key_insight: A minimizing-movement framework uses a convex surrogate energy to construct parametric finite element schemes with unique one-step solutions and discrete energy dissipation.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports energy-consistent simulation of anisotropic interface motion, including area-preserving evolution relevant to materials microstructure modeling.
method: Majorize the anisotropic energy with a smooth, convex surrogate matching it at the current iterate.
Minimize at each time step using parametric finite elements of any fixed degree.
Use convex splitting for strong anisotropy and a scalar constraint for area preservation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments show approximately expected convergence in smooth isotropic and weakly anisotropic cases, energy dissipation, and area preservation.
watch_item: Strongly anisotropic tests develop mesh-scale oscillations under refinement; one-step uniqueness also requires a nonvanishing current-curve derivative on every element.
paper_title: A minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening flows
